name: std::future_error::future_error
intro:
1) Copy constructor. Initializes the contents of the new future_error object with those of other. If *this and other both have dynamic type std::future_error then std::strcmp(what(), other.what()) == 0.

2) Constructs a new future_error object containing the error code std::make_error_code(ec).

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
other

 -

 another future_error object to copy


 ec

 -

 error code

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: There is no standard-compliant way for the user to construct a future_error other than copying from another future_error prior to C++17. C++11 and C++14 depict an exposition-only public constructor taking a std::error_code, and some implementations provide such a constructor.
